idiom_name: protocol in a separate module + existential or generic use
implementation_notes: A protocol declares the contract and can live in its own SwiftPM library target that the client imports, while the conforming type stays in the implementation module. Clients use it either as a generic constraint (some Clock, C: Clock) or as an existential (any Clock); the existential is the runtime-substitutable form and adds a box. Use generics when the concrete type is fixed at compile time and any P when implementations are selected at runtime.
pitfalls: A protocol with Self or associated-type requirements cannot be used as a type (the existential does not conform to itself), forcing a generic solution or type erasure.
Existentials box the value and dispatch through a witness table, which costs an allocation and an indirection per call.
Retroactive conformance added in an extension cannot override an existing conformance's behaviour for the same type.
